model_paper_title: Class 7 Mathematics Model Test Paper - Chapter 6: Number Play

questions.question: What is the parity of the sum of an Even integer and an Odd integer?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Even (2m) + Odd (2n + 1) = 2(m + n) + 1, which is always Odd. [1 Mark]

questions.question: What is the parity of the sum of page numbers on any single two-sided leaf torn from a book?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Front page is 2k-1 (odd) and back page is 2k (even). Sum = 4k - 1, which is always Odd. [1 Mark]

questions.question: In a 3x3 magic square filled with numbers 1 to 9, what is the invariant magic sum S of each row?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Total sum = 45. Each of 3 rows = 45 / 3 = 15. [1 Mark]

questions.question: What must be the value of the center cell x in a 3x3 magic square of numbers 1 to 9?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Center cell x = Magic constant / 3 = 15 / 3 = 5. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The first child standing in a single-file line always calls out 0 under the taller-in-front rule.
Reason (R): Nobody is standing ahead of the first child, so the count of taller people in front is 0.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Count of people in front is 0. Both A and R are true and R explains A. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The sum of 50 odd integers is always an even integer.
Reason (R): Adding an even number of odd integers yields an even sum because odd numbers pair up into even sums.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: 50 is even. Sum of an even number of odd integers is always even. [1 Mark]

questions.question: Determine the overall parity of: Sum of 3 odd numbers and 2 even numbers.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Step 1: Sum of 3 odd numbers = Odd. [1 Mark]
Step 2: Sum of 2 even numbers = Even.
Total = Odd + Even = Odd. [1 Mark]

questions.question: In a line of children, height callout values are (0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 3). Which position holds the tallest child?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Any child calling out 0 has nobody taller in front. The absolute tallest child in the group must call out 0 and can be at position 1 or 2 depending on order. [2 Marks]

questions.question: Write algebraic representations for (i) any even integer and (ii) any odd integer.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) Even integer = 2n where n is an integer. [1 Mark]
(ii) Odd integer = 2n - 1 (or 2n + 1) where n is an integer. [1 Mark]

questions.question: How many distinct 3x3 magic squares can be formed using digits 1 to 9 including rotations and reflections?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: There are 8 distinct magic squares (1 primary arrangement + 3 rotations + 4 reflections). [2 Marks]

questions.question: Prove why front page 2k-1 and back page 2k on a book leaf sum to 4k-1.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Sum = (2k - 1) + 2k = 4k - 1. Since 4k is even, 4k - 1 is odd. [2 Marks]

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer Questions / Numerical Proofs)

questions.question: Prove algebraically why the center cell 'x' of a 3x3 magic square filled with numbers 1 to 9 must equal 5.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Step 1: Total sum of digits 1 to 9 = 45. Magic constant S = 45 / 3 = 15. [1 Mark]
Step 2: The center cell x belongs to 4 lines: Row 2, Column 2, Main Diagonal 1, Main Diagonal 2. [1 Mark]
Step 3: Summing all 4 lines gives 4 * S = 4 * 15 = 60. [1 Mark]
Step 4: In this sum, every cell is counted once except x which is counted 4 times:
  45 + 3x = 60 => 3x = 15 => x = 5. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
A 2x3 grid has cells filled with integers to satisfy row/column parity requirements:
- Row 1 sum must be EVEN.
- Row 2 sum must be ODD.
- Column 1 sum must be ODD.
- Column 2 sum must be EVEN.
- Column 3 sum must be EVEN.
Construct a valid Even/Odd assignment grid.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Grid template:
  Row 1: [Even, Even, Even] -> Sum = Even. [1.5 Marks]
  Row 2: [Odd, Even, Even] -> Sum = Odd. [1.5 Marks]
Check columns:
  Col 1: Even + Odd = Odd (Valid). [0.3 Mark]
  Col 2: Even + Even = Even (Valid). [0.3 Mark]
  Col 3: Even + Even = Even (Valid). [0.4 Mark]

questions.case_scenario:
Case Study: Height Line Callout Logic
Eight children stand in a single-file line. Each child reports the number of children standing in front who are strictly taller than them.

sub_questions.sub_q: (a) What is the maximum possible callout number in a group of 8 children?
sub_questions.solution: Max callout = 7, called out by the shortest child standing at the end. [1.5 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (b) What callout number will the tallest child in the group always report, regardless of position?
(c) If callout numbers are (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7), describe the relative height arrangement of the line.
sub_questions.solution: The children are arranged in strictly decreasing order of height from front to back (tallest at front, shortest at back). [3 Marks]
